<meta>continues from previous page: ...which God has</meta> destined for them, so that they might penetrate [the diseases]. From these things, gather that it is necessary that [the healing process] should proceed according to my prescription, and by no means according to yours. Here it is necessary that you follow me, not I you. And although you may thunder many things against me even now, my Monarchy shall nonetheless stand, while yours will perish entirely. I do not write about Alchemy so prolixly in vain, but I do this with this mind and purpose: that you might know closely and solidly from these things what lies within it, and how it ought to be understood. Nor should you be offended by the fact that neither gold nor silver is produced from it. But rather, this must be taken care of: that through it, secrets <term>arcana</term> <gloss>mysteries/powerful medicinal agents</gloss> are discovered, and the deceits of the <term>seplasiariorum</term> <gloss>perfumers/apothecaries (often used pejoratively by Paracelsus)</gloss> are exposed, by which the crude masses are deceived while they provide them, for one florin, what they would not redeem for a single coin. So precious are their secrets.

<margin>Poison also in the best things.</margin>
Who is there who would dare to deny that poison hides and exists even in the best things? Everyone is forced to admit this. If this is true, then, I ask you: should poison not be separated from the good and the useful? And the good taken, and the evil left behind? Indeed, it must be so. If, therefore, it must be so: I ask you to tell me, how is it separated in your workshops? For among you, all things remain mixed. But so that you may defend your simplicity, if you are convicted of admitting that poison hides there and you are asked where it eventually goes, then I do not know what you bring forth regarding "corrections," which supposedly extract and remove the poison,
<margin>The correction of physicians is ventilated.</margin>
just as they correct Quince or Scammony, after Diagridium <note>a purgative preparation of scammony</note> is named. But what kind of "correction" is that? Does the poison not remain afterwards just as it was at first? And yet, you meanwhile boast that you have corrected it, so that the poison no longer harms. But where has it gone? 
<margin>Diagridium.</margin>
It remains in the Diagridium. Test that, if you are wise: exceed the measure, and you will see where the poison is. For you will know it quite briskly. Thus you also correct Turbith <note>a type of purgative root</note>, and call it <term>Diaturbith</term> <gloss>a preparation of turbith</gloss>. Such are your "corrections," which would suit rustics and should be fed to horses. Make an experiment by exceeding the measure, and increase the dose: you will see whether or not you will feel the poison. 
<margin>What it is to correct a medicine</margin>
*To correct is to take the corrected.* If a man is malicious and has sinned, if he is punished, the correction does not extend further than the will of the one who has been punished lasts. Such are these corrections of yours too; it is situated within the things themselves, not within you. Now, in this case, a physician must consider nothing more than that the poison should be removed. This must be done through separation: as, for example, a serpent is poisonous, and yet it is adopted into food. If you remove the poison from it, you may eat it with no harm. The same must be understood regarding all other things equally, namely, that a similar separation is necessary. That not having been done, you cannot be secure in your operation, unless by chance it happens that nature supplies your turns, or a greater kindness of heaven favors you. For in your art, no protection will remain.

Now, therefore, if that true foundation is required which removes the poison, how does Alchemy provide it? For it is necessary that this be done so that, if Mars <note>the alchemical sign for iron</note> is in the Sun <note>the alchemical sign for gold</note>, Mars should be removed; and if Saturn <note>the alchemical sign for lead</note> dwells in Venus <note>the alchemical sign for copper</note>, it should be separated from it. For as many ascendants and impressions as there are in the things of nature, so many bodies exist in them. But as for those bodies that are contrary, it is necessary that some part of them be entirely removed and taken away, so that in this way all contrariety is removed, and the evil that you seek is taken away from the good.
<margin>Fire perfects all things.</margin>
Just as gold is useful for nothing unless it is first cast into the fire, so much less useful is medicine that does not pass through fire. For it is necessary that all things pass through fire into another generation, which ought to lead to and assist man. And should this not deservedly be considered the honest foundation of any physician? For a physician ought not to apply poisons, but true secrets. 
<margin>Workshops criticized.</margin>
However, all those workshop preparations, as many of them as there are, do not contribute even a single letter to this teaching. But they are occupied simply in "correcting," as if a dog were to fart in a room, and that stench were to be quieted either by lozenges and incense, or by juniper wood; does the stench not remain in the room just as much after as before, I ask? And although it might not be perceived by smell, is one therefore allowed to say that the stench has been separated and remains no longer? Indeed, it is present, but "corrected" by the smoke. Thus, therefore, the smoke and the stench enter the nostrils together. Of such a kind also are the corrections of the apothecaries, who dull <term>Aleopaticum</term> <gloss>a specific medicinal compound</gloss> with sugar, so that it might inflict no harm. Thus sugar and honey are their "mastery." Thus they also "correct" Gentian with theriac. But are these not works of asinine ignorance? Yet they boast and sell themselves as the chief physicians. But who is so stupid as not to smell immediately that these things are worth nothing? Regarding their remedies, I ask what else they can boast of, other than to say, *This Electuary is sweet, [made] of aromatics, [and] sugar,*

<summary>Paracelsus condemns the "corrections" practiced by traditional apothecaries as superficial masking of toxins rather than true alchemical separation. He argues that only through fire and chemical separation can a substance's inherent poison be removed and its true medicinal potential (arcana) be realized.</summary>
<keywords>Alchemy, Pharmacy, Toxin, Correction, Arcana, Paracelsus, Separation, Fire</keywords>
